body:
Yeah, I considered your approach at one point.  If you run the tests, you'll see this breaks existing unit tests, which is why I didn't go with it:

`test_fuzzy_search.cpp:48`:
```
	// Short query, many matches, few adjacent characters
	{ "///gd", "./menu/hud/hud.gd" },
```

Your version does not score `./menu/hud/hud.gd` highest for the search `///gd` but instead scores `./menu/menu/characters/dead_guy/dead_guy.gd` highest, like this:

`.[/]menu[/]menu[/]characters/dead_[g]uy/[d]ead_guy.gd`

The `[d]` earns a +4 bonus for being a substring of the `///gd` token that matches at the start of a filename!

I was so surprised by this outcome that I decided it would be better to not yet attempt solving this more general case of "user starts to type filename then jumps ahead in filename and is superseded by shorter path that also has both words on word boundaries" :)

As to rewriting the system to address broader concerns, I'd argue that goes against Godot's [Best Practices for Engine Contribution](https://contributing.godotengine.org/en/latest/engine/guidelines/best_practices.html).

Edit to add - the `menu__debug` search case could *possibly* be resolved in the future by giving a score bonus to matches (exact or inexact) at the start of the filename, but only when they are the first substring in the `FuzzyTokenMatch.substrings` vector.  But I'd want a lot more test cases to show that this doesn't have unexpected behavior like the above proposed change.
